questions.question: A sum of money at compound interest amounts to seven times of itself in 3 years. In how many year will it be 2401 times of itself?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

A sum amounts to 7 times itself in 3 years

**Formula used:**

Amount = Principal ×(1 +Rate/100)ⁿ

Where n = number of years

**Calculation:**

Let P be the sum of money and R = rate %

Amount after 3 years,

7P = P(1 + R/100)³

⇒ 7 = (1 + R/100)³ ---(1)

Let after 't' years amount becomes 2401 times of sum

2401 × P = P(1 + R/100)t 

⇒ 2401 = (1 + R/100)t 

⇒ 7⁴ = (1 + R/100)t ---(2)

On comparing (1) and (2) we get,

(1 + R/100)¹² = (1 + R/100)t

⇒ t = 12

**∴ After 12 years the sum will become 2401 times of itself.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** [IMAGE: https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/VnpydsfhbFlaZ5pOg1aDWNp0AcJ1CM1Ir9H-XCUwpv2tFt6Ef3O6Dc5-q_6XBsKhtCHPrb_FqFcTArnGY_sN-W3NwFT4vD_m235NUdr0fcgxrDi2fvI3odFQz7eV5ZtuzDeNXAb7wHSv6J-bk6_slEE] 

In the first 3 years, the amount becomes 7 times of principal

In the next 3 years, the amount becomes (7 × 7) 0r 7² times of principal

Hence, the amount becomes 7⁴ times of the principal in = 4 × 3 = 12 years

**∴ The sum becomes 2401 times itself in 12 years.**

questions.question: A man covers two-third of a certain distance at the speed of 70 km/h and the rest at the speed of 50 km/h. It takes him {6(4)/(5)} hours for the whole journey. At a speed of 56 km/h, in what time will he be able to cover the entire distance?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total time = 6(4)/(5) = (34)/(5) hrs

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between the two points be '3X'

The person travels 2X distance with a speed of 70 km/h

He travels the remaining X distance with a speed of 50 km/h

Using the formula, for the whole journey

34/5 = 2X/70 + X/50

⇒ 34/5 = 17X/350

⇒ X = 2 × 70 = 140 km

∴ Distance (3X) = 140 × 3 = 420km

Time taken to travel this distance with a speed of 56 km/h,

Time = 420/56 = 15/2

Or Time = 7(1)/(2) hrs.

**∴ Time taken to travel the complete distance will be 7(1)/(2) hrs.**

questions.question: In a family 5 people spend 10% on the purchase of sugar. The price of sugar increased by 10%. What should be the percentage decrease in the consumption of sugar so as not to increase the expenditure?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The price of sugar is increased by 10%

**Formula used:**

Expenditure = Price × Quantity

Percentage reduction in a Quantity = (Old quantity - New quantity)/Old quantity × 100

**Calculation:**

If Price is increased in ratio a : b

Then, to keep the expenditure same 

The quantity should be reduced in the ratio b : a

Here, price is increaseby 10% 

Ratio of price change = 10 : 11

⇒ Ratio of quantity = 11 : 10

Reduction in quantity = (11 - 10)/11 = 1/11

Percent reduction in quantity = 1/11 × 100 = 9(1)/(11)%

**∴ Percentage decrease in the consumption of sugar so as to not increase the expenditure is 9(1)/(11)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** Let the price of sugar be 100

Increase price of sugar = 100 × 1.1 = 110 (∵ 10% increase)

Let the initial quantity of sugar purchased = 10

Old expenditure on sugar = 100 × 10 = 1000

New expenditure = Increased price × New quantity

Keeping the expenditure same

⇒ 1000 = 110 × New quantity

⇒ New quantity = 100/11

Percentage Reduction in quantity = (10 - 100/11)/10 × 100 

⇒ (110 - 100)/110 × 100

⇒ 1/11 × 100

⇒ 9(1)/(11)%

∴ Percentage decrease in consumption is 9(1)/(11)%.

questions.question: Varun bought a curtain cloth from a wholesaler at 20% discount on the marked price. He then marked the cloth at 20% higher than the original marked price and allowed 10% discount. What is his percentage profit?
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

Profit % = (P / CP) × 100

Where, 

CP = Cost price 

P = Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Selling price = Marked Price x ( 100 - Discount)/100

**Calculation:**

Let the Marked Price set by the Wholesaler be 100

Cost price (CP) for Varun = 100 x (100 - 20)/100 = 80 (∵ 20% discount)

**Note: Discount always gives on marked price. **

Marked Price (MP) set by Varun = 100 × (100 + 20)/100 = 120

(∵ 20% higher than the original marked price)

Selling Price (SP) of Varun = 120 x (100 - 10)/100 = 108 (∵ 10% discount)

Profit % of Varun = (108 - 80)/80 × 100 = 35%

**∴ Profit % of Varun is 35%**

questions.question: Find the single discount equivalent to two successive discounts of 25% and 10%.

D% = D1 + D2 - D1 × D2/100

**∴ The single discount equivalent is 32.5%.**

The two successive discounts are 25% and 10%

questions.question: For a certain sum, in 2 years, the simple interest is Rs. 80 and the compound interest for the same period at the same rate of interest is Rs. 85. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Compound interest for two years = Rs. 85

Simple interest for two years = Rs. 80

**Formula used**

Simple interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Where P = Principal amount, R = Rate, T = Time** **

**Concept used:**

Simple interest (SI) is the rate percent of the principal amount

In compound interest, the principal modifies every year. The interest of the previous year becomes the principal for the following year.

For example, 

Let SI (for 1 year) = Rs. X, Rate % = R

Then, CI (for 2 years) = X + X + R % of X

Or, CI (for 2 years) = SI for 2 years + R % × SI for 1 year

**Calculation:**

SI for 1 year = 80 ÷ 2 = Rs. 40

CI (for 2 years) = SI for 2 years + R % × SI for 1 year

85 = 80 + R % × 40

⇒ R % × 40 = 5

⇒ R × 40 ÷ 100 = 5

⇒ R = (25)/(2) 

⇒ R = 12.5 %

**∴ The rate of interest per annum is 12.5%.**

questions.question: Pipes A nd B can fill a tank in 18 hours and 27 hours, respectively. If both the pipes are opened on alternate hours, one at a time, and pipe A is opened for the first hour, then in how many hours will the tank be filled completely?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by pipe A = 18 hrs

Time taken by pipe B = 27 hrs

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total work done/ total time taken

**Calculation:**

Let the total volume of the tank be the LCM of 18 and 27 i.e. 54 unit

The efficiency of A = 54/18 = 3

Efficiency of B = 54/27 = 2

Tank filled by both pipes together in 2 days (A starts the work) = 3 +2 = 5 unit

Tank filled by both pipes together in 20 days = 50 unit

Now, on the 21st day, A will fill 3 units of tank

Total tank filled till now = 53 unit

On the 22ⁿd day, B will work and will fill 2 units of the tank, but we need only 1 unit of more work. Hence B will work only half a day

Total number of days taken = 21(1)/(2) days

**∴ The total number of days taken by A and B together to fill the tank completely is 21(1)/(2) days**

questions.question: How many maximum litres of milk can a hemispherical bowl of diameter 9 cm hold approximately?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of hemisphere = 9 cm

Radius = 9/2 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of hemisphere = 2/3 × π × r³

Where r = radius of hemisphere

**Calculation:**

Volume (V) = 2/3 × π × (9/2)³

⇒ V = 2/3 × 22/7 × (9/2)³

⇒ V = 190.92 cm³

⇒ V = 0.191 litres (∵ 1 litre = 1000 cm³)

**∴ The bowl can hold 0.191 litres of milk**

⇒ Volume ∝ r² × h

where, r = radius of cone

h = height of cone

⇒ Volume of cone C ∝ (2x)² × (3x)

Radius of cone D = 3x, height of cone D = 2y

⇒ Volume of cone D : volume of cone C = 18x²y : 12x²y = 3 : 2

**∴ The ratio of cone D to that of cone C is 3 : 2**

questions.question: By selling 90 pens for Rs. 1,557, a shopkeeper loses 30%. How many pens should he sell for Rs. 708 so as to earn a profit of 18%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The selling price of 90 pens = Rs. 1557

Loss % = 30%

**Formula used:**

Profit % = (SP - CP)/CP × 100

Loss % = (CP - SP)/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

Selling price (SP) of 90 pens = 1557

Loss % = 30%

∴ Cost Price (CP) of 90 pens = (1557 × 100)/(100 - 30) 

⇒ CP of 90 pens = 15570/7

⇒ CP of 1 pen = 15570/(7 × 90)

⇒ CP of 1 pen = Rs. 173/7

Let P pens be sold to earn a profit of 18%

CP of P pens = 173P/7

SP of P pens = Rs. 708

⇒ Profit % of P pens = (SP of P pens - CP of P pens)/(CP of P pens) × 100

⇒ 18 = (708 - 173P/7)/(173P/7) × 100

⇒ 18 = (708 × 7/173P - 1) × 100

⇒ 118 = 708 × 7 × 100/173P

⇒ P = (708 × 7 × 100)/(173 × 118)

⇒ P = 24.27

∵ The number of Pens cannot be in decimal, we take the value of P as the nearest integer i.e. P = 24

**∴ 24 Pens should be sold for Rs. 708 so as to earn a profit of 18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Formula used:**

Let N1 = initial number of items, P1 % or L1 % = initial Profit % or Loss %, SP1 = initial Selling Price

And, N2 = final number of items, P2 % or L2 % = final Profit % or Loss %, SP2 = final Selling price

Then the relation between the two is given by

In case of Profit % is given

⇒ [N1 × (100 + P1 %)]/SP1 = [N2 × (100 + P2 %)]/SP2 

If Loss % is given

⇒ [N1 × (100 - L1 %)]/SP1 = [N2 × (100 - L2 %)]/SP2

**Calculation:**

N1 = 90, L1 = 30%, SP1 = Rs. 1557

N2 = P (Let), P2 = 18%, SP2 = 708

⇒ (90 × 70)/1557 = (P × 118)/708

⇒ P = 24.27 

∴ 24 pens should be sold

questions.question:
Find the least number which is a perfect square and is divisible by each of the following numbers.

15, 24 and 36
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Given numbers are 15, 24 and 36

**Formula used:**

The Least common multiple (LCM) of two or more numbers is the least number which is exactly divisible by each of those numbers.

**Calculation:**

The least number which is divisible by each of 15, 24 and 36 will be the LCM of 15, 24 and 36

LCM of 15, 24, and 36 

15 = 3 × 5

24 = 3 × 2 × 2 × 2

36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3

LCM of 15, 24, and 36 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 360

Clearly, we can see that to make 360 a perfect square number we have to multiply it by 2 and 5, then we get

⇒ 360 × 2 × 5 = 3600

**∴ The least number which is a perfect square and is divisible by each of 15, 24, and 36 is 3600.**

questions.question: A motorcar started with a speed of 60 km/h, and its speed is increased by 20 km/h every 3 hour. How many hours will it take to cover a distance of 470 km?
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

According to the question;

For 3 hours, Speed = 60 km/hr

Distance covered in two hours = 60 × 3 = 180 km

For next 3 hours, Speed = 60 km/hr + 20 km/hr = 80 km/hr

Distance covered in next 3 hours = 80 × 3 = 240 km

Distance covered in 6 hours = 180 km + 240 km = 420km

Remaining Distance = 470 - 420 = 50 km

Now, speed = 80 + 20 = 100 km/hr

Now, Time = 50/100 = 1/2 hr

Total Time = 3 hr + 3 hr + 1/2 hr = 6 (1)/(2)hr.

**∴ The required answer will be **6 (1)/(2) **hr.**
